# Synced Flow documentation

> Developer and AI-agent documentation for Synced Flow, an AI-native fluid CSS design system.

Synced Flow gives developers and coding agents a shared styling contract: design tokens, layout primitives, native components, recipe markup, generated utility CSS, and CLI verification.

## Agent rules

When using Synced Flow in a project:

1. Inspect the project before editing.
2. Install and initialise Synced Flow with the matching preset.
3. Put brand decisions in `synced-flow.config.mjs` theme tokens before writing one-off CSS.
4. Prefer `sf-container`, `sf-section`, `sf-stack`, `sf-cluster`, `sf-auto-grid`, `sf-split`, and `sf-sidebar` for layout.
5. Prefer `sf-button`, `sf-card`, `sf-badge`, `sf-field`, and `sf-input` for common UI.
6. Use semantic utility names such as `bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `bg-primary`, `text-primary-foreground`, `border-border`, and `bg-surface`.
7. Keep class names complete in source files. Do not build class names from string fragments.
8. Use `safelist` only when dynamic classes are unavoidable.
9. Do not enable `responsiveVariants` in new projects unless explicitly migrating breakpoint-prefixed classes.
10. Run verification before finishing.

## Useful commands

```bash
pnpm add @synced/flow
pnpm exec synced-flow init --preset next --agents
pnpm exec synced-flow tokens --json
pnpm exec synced-flow catalog --json
pnpm exec synced-flow pattern --list
pnpm exec synced-flow suggest "service site with pricing and faq"
pnpm exec synced-flow lint --json
pnpm exec synced-flow doctor
```

## Common finish checklist

```bash
pnpm flow:build
pnpm flow:check
pnpm exec synced-flow lint --json
pnpm flow:doctor
```
